headline_marked: After 45 years, [[Ziaur Rahman murder convict arrested]] in Dhaka
headline: After 45 years, Ziaur Rahman murder convict arrested in Dhaka
summary: Major (retd) Mozzaffar Hossain, one of the primary suspects in the 1981 assassination of President Ziaur Rahman, was detained by DB police in Banani.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) police have detained Major (retd) Mozzaffar Hossain, who had been on the run for 45 years in connection with the murder of former President Ziaur Rahman.
He was arrested at midnight on Wednesday from the Banani DOHS area of the capital. Following legal procedures, he has been handed over to the army for a court-martial.
The assassination took place on May 30, 1981, when a group of rogue army officers attacked the Chittagong Circuit House in the early hours of the morning.
According to the case details, Major Mozzaffar Hossain was the one who first identified President Ziaur Rahman and fired directly at him.
After confirming the kill, he reportedly phoned Major General Abul Manzur, the then GOC of the 24th Infantry Division at Chittagong Cantonment, to announce, 'The President has been killed.'
While others, including Major General Abul Manzur, were later arrested or killed during the army's operation to restore order, Captain Mosleh Uddin received a life sentence.
Major Mozzaffar Hossain and Major S.M. Khaled had managed to flee and remained fugitives until this arrest.
caption:
A 45-year manhunt ends. The man who reportedly fired the fatal shots at President Ziaur Rahman has been arrested.

Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) police have detained Major (retd) Mozzaffar Hossain, who had been on the run for 45 years in connection with the murder of former President Ziaur Rahman.

He was arrested at midnight on Wednesday from the Banani DOHS area of the capital. Following legal procedures, he has been handed over to the army for a court-martial.

The assassination took place on May 30, 1981, when a group of rogue army officers attacked the Chittagong Circuit House in the early hours of the morning.

According to the case details, Major Mozzaffar Hossain was the one who first identified President Ziaur Rahman and fired directly at him.

After confirming the kill, he reportedly phoned Major General Abul Manzur, the then GOC of the 24th Infantry Division at Chittagong Cantonment, to announce, 'The President has been killed.'

While others, including Major General Abul Manzur, were later arrested or killed during the army's operation to restore order, Captain Mosleh Uddin received a life sentence.

Major Mozzaffar Hossain and Major S.M. Khaled had managed to flee and remained fugitives until this arrest.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Somoy News

headline_marked: 306 more hospitalized as [[2 more die of dengue]] in 24 hours
headline: 306 more hospitalized as 2 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The total death toll for the year has reached 32, with Dhaka division reporting the highest number of fatalities.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), two people died of dengue in the last 24 hours, both in the Dhaka division.
A total of 306 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country during the same period.
Dhaka division saw the highest number of hospitalizations, with 95 patients admitted.
Other regions reported admissions: Chittagong (66), Barishal (58), Khulna (38), Rangpur (23), and Rajshahi and Mymensingh (13 each).
Since January 1, this year, the total number of dengue deaths in Bangladesh has risen to 32.
Dhaka division continues to be the most affected area, recording 17 deaths so far this year.
caption:
306 people hospitalized in a single day. Dengue continues to claim lives across Bangladesh.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), two people died of dengue in the last 24 hours, both in the Dhaka division.

A total of 306 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country during the same period.

Dhaka division saw the highest number of hospitalizations, with 95 patients admitted.

Other regions reported admissions: Chittagong (66), Barishal (58), Khulna (38), Rangpur (23), and Rajshahi and Mymensingh (13 each).

Since January 1, this year, the total number of dengue deaths in Bangladesh has risen to 32.

Dhaka division continues to be the most affected area, recording 17 deaths so far this year.
